chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: First instruments: timber blocks, Boy Scout drums, ukulele
summary: He tried timber blocks, field drums in the Boy Scouts, a school quartet and the ukulele, and mentions Sergeant Willis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: : Now, with that band did you start

No, actually I had -- I borrowed some things called temple blocks. Now, this would be -- well what Lionel Hampton used them, but it was made out of wood. Did you ever see those? Usually drummers would use those.
Well, tempe blocks, I've seen, yeah.
Yeah. Now, you thinking of those temple blocks like that?
No, this was like a xylophone.
Oh, no. I've seen the African ones.

Yeah, well, this was about -- there was about two octaves of that. And I started out trying to play that, you know. Picking up them things. I don't know whether I started out with that or not. Let me go back.
In the Boy Scouts I played drums. I played field

drums in the Boy Scouts. And all this time I was singing -- the school had organized a little quartet, and I was singing in the quartet. And the man interested me in getting a trumpet, and I already knew how to play a ukulele. So I don't know when I really began the --
Well, ukuleles were very popular then.
You could learn them really without instruction, just by playing those finger chords.

Yes. And we had a guy there who was really terrific, a Sergeant Willis. He was a drummer and a ukulele player. And he used to walk up and down the streets playing that ukulele. And there's such things as the blues, and say "Five foot two, Eyes of Blue, has Anybody Seen My Gal," you know.
